clue.text: Side path turning into a main road

indicators.note: turning into signals that the letters of side path are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A side path that bends round and becomes a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main road' looks like a highway, but 'main' is the sea and 'road' (roadstead) is a sheltered anchorage. SPITHEAD is the stretch of water off Portsmouth where the Royal Navy anchors.
explanation.definitionFit: Spithead is a famous naval anchorage, and a road or roadstead is sheltered water where ships ride at anchor on the main, the sea.

clue.text: Head of school caught by mob in disorderly struggle

indicators.note: Head of picks out the opening letter of school

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A headteacher is seized by an unruly crowd in a scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrabble is a scramble or scuffle, a frantic disorderly contest for something.

clue.text: Become liable to debts without interest

parts.note: to incur is to become liable to a cost or penalty
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Running up debts with no interest charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without interest' sounds financial, but it means lacking curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Incurious means lacking curiosity, showing no wish to know.

clue.text: Field division that may take years to train

definitions.text: Field division that may take years to train

parts.words: Field division that may take years to train
parts.note: a living boundary between fields of shrubs that are cut and laid over many seasons to make it thick, rather than an army unit in the field

explanation.surface: A military division in the field needing years of training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field division' suggests an army formation that needs training; it is a boundary of bushes, trained by laying and clipping.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a row of shrubs dividing fields, grown and shaped over many years.

clue.text: Publicise wine 'where it's duty-free

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Advertising wine at a duty-free shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Duty-free shops are found at the departure lounges of air terminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Duty-free shopping is a feature of international air terminals.

clue.text: Town and gown

explanation.surface: A rhyming pair, the university and the townsfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town and gown' is the stock phrase for townsfolk versus university members; here each word is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mantua is an Italian city, and a mantua is also a loose seventeenth-century woman's dress.

clue.text: Aphrodite's emaciated form

indicators.note: form here is a verb, to shape, so the letters of the goddess's name are reshaped

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The goddess of love's body looks skeletal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' reads as Aphrodite's figure but is the anagram signal; the possessive 's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophied means wasted away from lack of use or nourishment, as in a shrunken limb.

clue.text: Junk food

explanation.surface: Junk food.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'junk food' splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is rubbish or nonsense, and also the edible stomach lining of a cow.

clue.text: Female articles

parts.note: an is the indefinite article before a vowel
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Items of women's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female articles' suggests women's goods, but it is a woman's name built from three grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Property of the Oriental Express

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
to express something is to state it

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the Orient Express train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental Express' suggests the famous train; split it into E (east) and STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a person's land or total property.

clue.text: Competed in speed with one in the highway

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a highway
an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A racer took part in a speed contest on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to compete in a contest of speed.

clue.text: About to teach the others self-control

indicators.note: About here means going round, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: the rest are the others
to train someone is to teach them

explanation.surface: Someone is just going to teach the others how to control themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' is the signal that one word goes round the other; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is holding oneself back, a synonym for self-control.

clue.text: A lone crab scuttles round by the sea in Spain

indicators.note: a crab that scuttles round moves about, so the letters of a lone crab are jumbled

explanation.surface: A solitary crab runs about on a Spanish beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the Catalan city on Spain's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Man on board with a gun

explanation.surface: A man aboard ship carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship, but it is a chessboard; 'with' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman is a piece, and piece is also slang for a pistol or rifle.

clue.text: Cave used as an observation post

explanation.surface: A cave used by soldiers as a place to watch from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' is not a hollow in rock but the Latin schoolboy warning 'beware!' (two syllables), once shouted when a teacher approached.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave! is a warning cry like look out!, and a lookout is also a watchtower or vantage point for keeping watch.

clue.text: Goal likely to appear in breach of the rules

definitions.note: the answer is used as a verbal noun, the act of breaking rules

indicators.note: in places the goal word inside the phrase for likely to appear

parts.note: something in the offing is likely to appear soon
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A goal is likely to be scored in breach of the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads; 'likely to appear' comes from the idiom 'in the offing', and 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Offending is the act of transgressing, i.e. breaking a law or code.

clue.text: Miracle drug for backside in trouble

annotationWithheld.why: Miracle drug for backside in trouble (6): ELIXIR fits 'Miracle drug', but no reading of 'for backside in trouble' as printed (scan agrees) gives ELIXIR or its remaining letters, and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Miracle drug for backside in trouble

clue.text: Starting place for the three-legged race?

definitions.text: Starting place for the three-legged race?

parts.words: Starting place for the three-legged race?
parts.note: the race here is a people, not a sports-day event: the island whose flag shows three legs is where its inhabitants come from

explanation.surface: Where the sports-day three-legged race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx emblem, the triskelion, is three armoured legs joined at the thigh; the island lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx people originate on that island, whose symbol is three running legs.

clue.text: Service initiations

parts.note: church services by which people are welcomed into the faith, read as if it meant starting military service

explanation.surface: Recruits beginning their time in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests the armed forces; it is a church service, and the initiation is into the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening rites admit a person into the Christian church with water.

clue.text: Functional American fuel product

indicators.note: a product is something made from material, so the letters of fuel are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Describes an American fuel that works well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functional serves a practical purpose, which is to say it is handy.

clue.text: Gale blows itself out to a smooth finish

indicators.note: a gale that blows itself out is scattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A storm dies down to a calm ending.
explanation.walkthrough: In music LEGATO marks notes played smoothly joined; 'finish' here is the manner of the playing.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction meaning smooth and connected, without breaks between notes.

clue.text: Clergy in session here liaised with unorthodox movement

indicators.note: unorthodox movement means the letters of liaised are moved around irregularly

explanation.surface: Priests in a meeting collaborated with an unconventional religious movement.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDILIA are the stone seats in a church chancel's south wall where the officiating clergy sit during parts of the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedilia are seats beside the altar used by priests during Mass, so clergy sit there while the service is in session.

clue.text: View-from the flats

explanation.surface: The view from the flat apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flats' are not apartments but the painted canvas frames that make up a theatre set.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery means a landscape or vista, and in a theatre the painted backdrops and flats.

clue.text: We'd be lost without them!.

parts.note: the gushing compliment is read literally, as the people who stop a party of tourists from losing its way

explanation.surface: A heartfelt thank-you to indispensable helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who lead and show the way keep travellers from going astray.

clue.text: Abraham's birthplace has bar situated in town

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees is named in Genesis as the home of Abraham
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: The town where Abraham was born has a bar in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes what is located in a city rather than the country.

clue.text: Man-of-war rounds the point for : shelter

indicators.note: rounds means goes round, so the fighter's word encircles the compass point

parts.note: a Boer was a fighter in the Boer War, a man of that war
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A warship sails round the headland to find shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man-of-war' looks like a warship; it is a man of the (Boer) War. The stray colon before 'shelter' is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a shady arbour or leafy retreat in a garden.

clue.text: A cottager going out may wear it

definitions.text: A cottager going out may wear it

indicators.note: going out here suggests the letters of a cottager leave their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from a cottage would put this on to go outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a countryman stepping out on a cold day would wear this heavy coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat worn outdoors, the sort a country dweller puts on to go out.

clue.text: Descriptive of great sea-power

parts.note: not naval might but the moon-driven rise and fall of the ocean, the force of its ebb and flow

explanation.surface: An adjective for a mighty navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-power' suggests a navy; it is the power of the sea itself in its rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes the ebb and flow of the ocean, whose surges are enormously powerful.

clue.text: Feathers tipped in blue

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathers of a bird
a dump is a tip for rubbish, so whatever is tipped there ends up among the ...

explanation.surface: Feathers dyed blue at the ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped in blue' reads as coloured at the tips; instead 'tipped in' means put on the rubbish tip, i.e. in the dumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low, and down in the dumps is an idiom for being dejected.

clue.text: See 27
Suckers in starting price swindles

parts.note: SP is the racing abbreviation for starting price, the final odds on a horse
rigs are frauds or swindles

explanation.surface: Gullible punters are caught in betting frauds at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' looks like dupes, but it means shoots growing from a plant; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Suckers and sprigs are both small shoots or twigs from a plant.

clue.text: Rides round on whirlwinds

indicators.note: round says the word for rides goes about the other piece

parts.note: cycles are bike rides

explanation.surface: Someone is riding round on whirlwinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclones are violent storms of rotating wind, a large kind of whirlwind.
